title: Crime, inland marine, equipment breakdown and farm
summary: Crime definitions, insuring agreements and triggers; the Nationwide Marine Definition and key inland marine forms; equipment breakdown; farm coverages A-J.
objectives: Tell robbery, burglary, safe burglary and theft apart
Compare the loss sustained and discovery crime forms
Name the marine classes and match common inland marine forms
Recall equipment breakdown valuation and the farm coverage letters

scenes.title: Crime, inland marine, equipment breakdown and farm
scenes.subtitle: Four more coverage parts with a few exam favorites each

beats.text: Four more coverage parts: crime, inland marine, equipment breakdown and farm. Each has a few exam favorites.
beats.say: Four more coverage parts: crime, inland marine, equipment breakdown and farm. Each has a few exam favorites.

scenes.title: Robbery, burglary, safe burglary, theft
scenes.src: ISO CR 00 21 11 15, F. defs. 20, 21, 23; IRMI glossary 'burglary'
items: Taking from a person by harm or threat
Unlawful entry into or exit from premises
Forcing a locked safe, or taking the safe
Any unlawful taking; the broadest term

beats.text: The 2015 crime form defines robbery as taking property from a person by someone who causes or threatens bodily harm, or commits an obviously unlawful act the person witnesses.
beats.say: The twenty fifteen crime form defines robbery as taking property from a person by someone who causes or threatens bodily harm, or commits an obviously unlawful act the person witnesses.

beats.text: Burglary, a glossary term, is theft from premises by someone who unlawfully enters or exits. Breaking out counts too.
beats.say: Burglary, a glossary term, is theft from premises by someone who unlawfully enters or exits. Breaking out counts too.

beats.text: Safe burglary is taking property from a locked safe, with marks of forced entry on its outside, or taking the safe itself.
beats.say: Safe burglary is taking property from a locked safe, with marks of forced entry on its outside, or taking the safe itself.

beats.text: Theft is any unlawful taking of property to the insured's loss. It's the broadest term.
beats.say: Theft is any unlawful taking of property to the insured's loss. It's the broadest term.

scenes.title: A bad week at a Flint party store
scenes.src: ISO CR 00 21 11 15, F. defs. 20, 21, 23; IRMI glossary 'burglary'; hook mn-mn_comm-11
scenes.story: A man points a gun at the clerk and takes the cash. A thief hides in the cooler after closing, then breaks out the back door with stock. Someone opens the safe with the right combination and takes the contents, leaving no marks.

items.label: Hid inside, broke out the back door
Safe opened by combination, no marks
items.detail: Not safe burglary: no marks of forced entry

scenes.answer: Robbery, burglary, and not a safe burglary. Every one of them is also a theft.

beats.text: Let's classify a bad week at a Flint party store. A man points a gun at the clerk and takes the cash. A thief hides in the cooler after closing, then breaks out the back door with stock.
beats.say: Let's classify a bad week at a Flint party store. A man points a gun at the clerk and takes the cash. A thief hides in the cooler after closing, then breaks out the back door with stock.

beats.text: And someone opens the safe with the right combination and takes the contents, leaving no marks. What is each one?
beats.say: And someone opens the safe with the right combination and takes the contents, leaving no marks. What is each one?

beats.text: The gun at the clerk is robbery: a person was threatened. The thief who broke out is a burglar: an unlawful exit counts.
beats.say: The gun at the clerk is robbery: a person was threatened. The thief who broke out is a burglar: an unlawful exit counts.

beats.text: The safe opened with no marks isn't a safe burglary. Still, every one of these is a theft.
beats.say: The safe opened with no marks isn't a safe burglary. Still, every one of these is a theft.

scenes.title: Crime insuring agreements: money vs property
scenes.src: ISO CR 00 21 11 15, A.1-7; the PSI outline lists computer fraud and funds transfer fraud separately (older editions)

beats.text: The 2015 crime form has seven insuring agreements. Employee Theft covers theft by employees of money, securities or other property.
beats.say: The twenty fifteen crime form has seven insuring agreements. Employee Theft covers theft by employees of money, securities or other property.

beats.text: Inside the premises, money and securities are covered for theft, disappearance or destruction. Other property, like merchandise, only for robbery of a custodian or safe burglary.
beats.say: Inside the premises, money and securities are covered for theft, disappearance or destruction. Other property, like merchandise, only for robbery of a custodian or safe burglary.

beats.text: Outside the premises, with a messenger or armored car company, money is covered the same way. Other property, only for robbery.
beats.say: Outside the premises, with a messenger or armored car company, money is covered the same way. Other property, only for robbery.

beats.text: Three more: Forgery or Alteration, Computer and Funds Transfer Fraud, and Money Orders and Counterfeit Money. The PSI outline lists the two fraud coverages separately.
beats.say: Three more: Forgery or Alteration, Computer and Funds Transfer Fraud, and Money Orders and Counterfeit Money. The P S I outline lists the two fraud coverages separately.

scenes.title: Loss sustained vs discovery
scenes.src: ISO CR 00 21 11 15, A., E.1.g; discovery: CR 00 22 05 06, E.1.j and Rough Notes PF&M 251.4-2 (CR 00 20 11 15 text not seen)

columns.name: Loss sustained form
points: Loss must occur during the policy period
Found during the policy or the extended period
Up to 1 year after cancellation to discover

columns.name: Discovery form
points: Loss may have occurred at any time
Must be discovered during the policy period
Up to 60 days after cancellation to discover

scenes.tell: Did it happen on my watch? Loss sustained. Did I find it on my watch? Discovery.

beats.text: Crime forms come with two triggers. The loss sustained form covers loss that occurs during the policy period. After cancellation, you get up to 1 year to discover it.
beats.say: Crime forms come with two triggers. The loss sustained form covers loss that occurs during the policy period. After cancellation, you get up to one year to discover it.

beats.text: The discovery form covers loss that occurred at any time, as long as you discover it during the policy period, or within 60 days after cancellation.
beats.say: The discovery form covers loss that occurred at any time, as long as you discover it during the policy period, or within sixty days after cancellation.

beats.text: Ask: did it happen on my watch, or did I find it on my watch? And don't swap the tails: 1 year for loss sustained, 60 days for discovery.
beats.say: Ask: did it happen on my watch, or did I find it on my watch? And don't swap the tails: one year for loss sustained, sixty days for discovery.

scenes.q: Mid-term, a business with a discovery-form crime policy discovers a theft from two years before the policy began. It had no earlier crime coverage, and no retroactive date applies. Is it covered?
choices: Yes, because it was discovered during the policy period
No, because it occurred before the policy began
Only if it was discovered within 60 days after the theft
scenes.why: The discovery form covers loss sustained at any time, as long as it is discovered during the policy period or the 60-day extended period.

beats.text: Try this. A business with a discovery-form crime policy discovers, mid-term, a theft from two years before the policy began. No retroactive date applies. Is it covered? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Try this. A business with a discovery-form crime policy discovers, mid-term, a theft from two years before the policy began. No retroactive date applies. Is it covered? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: Yes. The discovery form doesn't care when the loss happened, only that it was discovered during the policy period.
reveal.say: Yes. The discovery form doesn't care when the loss happened, only that it was discovered during the policy period.

items.label: Instrumentalities of transportation
items.detail: Bridges, tunnels, piers, pipelines, power lines, towers

items.label: Not buildings or their fixed contents

beats.text: On to inland marine. The Nationwide Marine Definition lists six classes. The first three are imports, exports, and domestic shipments.
beats.say: On to inland marine. The Nationwide Marine Definition lists six classes. The first three are imports, exports, and domestic shipments.

beats.text: Next, bridges, tunnels and other instrumentalities of transportation and communication, like piers, pipelines and towers. Then personal and commercial property floater risks.
beats.say: Next, bridges, tunnels and other instrumentalities of transportation and communication, like piers, pipelines and towers. Then personal and commercial property floater risks.

beats.text: Buildings and their fixed contents are not marine risks. Michigan's own statutory definition of marine insurance excludes buildings and their contents too.
beats.say: Buildings and their fixed contents are not marine risks. Michigan's own statutory definition of marine insurance excludes buildings and their contents too.

scenes.title: Inland marine forms: who needs which
scenes.src: IRMI glossary; Verisk Commercial Inland Marine and transportation program sheets (2022); ISO IH 00 68 12 13 (FC&S 2018)
items: Others' goods left for cleaning or repair
A contractor's own machinery and tools
A jeweler's stock and customers' jewelry
A trucker's liability for others' cargo

beats.text: Some inland marine forms. Bailees customers covers others' goods left for cleaning or repair, like at a dry cleaner. Contractors equipment covers a contractor's own machinery and tools.
beats.say: Some inland marine forms. Bailees customers covers others' goods left for cleaning or repair, like at a dry cleaner. Contractors equipment covers a contractor's own machinery and tools.

beats.text: An installation floater covers equipment a contractor is installing. Don't swap them.
beats.say: An installation floater covers equipment a contractor is installing. Don't swap them.

beats.text: Jewelers block covers a jeweler's stock. Motor truck cargo carriers coverage is a trucker's liability for others' cargo. Commercial articles covers cameras and musical instruments used commercially.
beats.say: Jewelers block covers a jeweler's stock. Motor truck cargo carriers coverage is a trucker's liability for others' cargo. Commercial articles covers cameras and musical instruments used commercially.

scenes.q: An electrical contractor is installing new lighting equipment it bought for a customer's building. Which inland marine coverage is designed for that equipment while it's being installed?
scenes.why: An installation floater covers property, usually equipment, being installed by a contractor. Contractors equipment covers the contractor's own machinery and tools.

beats.text: Quick check. An electrical contractor is installing new lighting equipment it bought for a customer's building. Which coverage is designed for that equipment during installation? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Quick check. An electrical contractor is installing new lighting equipment it bought for a customer's building. Which coverage is designed for that equipment during installation? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: The installation floater. Contractors equipment would cover the contractor's own tools, not what it's installing.
reveal.say: The installation floater. Contractors equipment would cover the contractor's own tools, not what it's installing.

scenes.title: Equipment breakdown
scenes.src: EB 00 20 01 13 and EB 99 59 as described by FC&S (2016); a newer edition may exist

items.label: A breakdown of covered equipment
items.detail: Boilers, machinery, electrical and communication equipment

items.label: Replacement cost unless the ACV endorsement
Coverage can be suspended
items.detail: On equipment found in a dangerous condition, by written notice

beats.text: Equipment breakdown, formerly boiler and machinery, covers a breakdown of covered equipment: boilers, machinery, and electrical and communication equipment.
beats.say: Equipment breakdown, formerly boiler and machinery, covers a breakdown of covered equipment: boilers, machinery, and electrical and communication equipment.

beats.text: It values property at replacement cost by default. Attaching the Actual Cash Value endorsement changes that to actual cash value.
beats.say: It values property at replacement cost by default. Attaching the Actual Cash Value endorsement changes that to actual cash value.

beats.text: And the insurer can immediately suspend coverage on equipment found in a dangerous condition, by written notice.
beats.say: And the insurer can immediately suspend coverage on equipment found in a dangerous condition, by written notice.

scenes.title: Farm coverages A through J
scenes.src: ISO FP 00 10 09 94 (letters A-G; 2016 forms keep them); FL 00 20 per FC&S (2013); FP 00 13 04 16 (FC&S 2017)

columns.name: Farm property: E to G
points: G: Other farm structures, like barns

columns.name: Farm liability: H to J
points: H: Bodily injury and property damage

scenes.tell: A to D are lettered like homeowners. H, I and J mirror CGL Coverages A, B and C.

beats.text: Last, farm. A through D are the farmhouse, lettered like homeowners: dwellings, other private structures, household personal property, and loss of use.
beats.say: Last, farm. A through D are the farmhouse, lettered like homeowners: dwellings, other private structures, household personal property, and loss of use.

beats.text: E is scheduled farm personal property, F is unscheduled, or blanket, farm personal property, and G is other farm structures, like barns.
beats.say: E is scheduled farm personal property, F is unscheduled, or blanket, farm personal property, and G is other farm structures, like barns.

beats.text: Farm liability uses H, I and J, which mirror CGL Coverages A, B and C.
beats.say: Farm liability uses H, I and J, which mirror C G L Coverages A, B and C.

beats.text: Two more favorites: Coverage F needs insurance of at least 80% of actual cash value. And livestock means cattle, sheep, swine, goats, horses, mules and donkeys, not poultry.
beats.say: Two more favorites: Coverage F needs insurance of at least eighty percent of actual cash value. And livestock means cattle, sheep, swine, goats, horses, mules and donkeys, not poultry.

scenes.q: Under the ISO farm property forms, which animal is NOT included in the definition of "livestock"?
scenes.why: Livestock means cattle, sheep, swine, goats, horses, mules and donkeys. Chickens are poultry, a separately defined term.

beats.text: Last one. Under the farm forms, which animal is not livestock? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Last one. Under the farm forms, which animal is not livestock? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: Chickens. They're poultry, which is defined separately. Goats, mules and swine are all livestock.
reveal.say: Chickens. They're poultry, which is defined separately. Goats, mules and swine are all livestock.

scenes.title: Key takeaways
items: Robbery needs a person; burglary needs unlawful entry or exit
Loss sustained: 1 year to discover. Discovery: 60 days
Marine classes exclude buildings and their fixed contents
Equipment breakdown pays replacement cost unless ACV endorsed
Farm: A to D farmhouse, E to G farm property, H to J liability

beats.text: Let's recap. Robbery needs a person; burglary needs an unlawful entry or exit. Loss sustained gives 1 year to discover; discovery gives 60 days.
beats.say: Let's recap. Robbery needs a person; burglary needs an unlawful entry or exit. Loss sustained gives one year to discover; discovery gives sixty days.

beats.text: Marine classes exclude buildings. Equipment breakdown pays replacement cost unless endorsed. And farm runs A to J.
beats.say: Marine classes exclude buildings. Equipment breakdown pays replacement cost unless endorsed. And farm runs A to J.
